archetype.name: Dual-Threat (pass-first)
archetype.definition: A quarterback who wins first with efficient, accurate passing from a run-heavy offense, while his legs are now mostly a scramble-driven escape valve rather than a weekly designed-run engine.

report.headline: Best per-dropback passer in the league, but on low volume and a bad ankle
report.take:
Four games in, Jackson leads all 42 qualifiers in adjusted net yards per dropback (10.74) and ranks second in yards per attempt and third in CPOE. That is efficiency, not volume. Baltimore throws less than game situations predict (25th in pass rate over expected), so he averages only 24 attempts a game. His passing yards rank 13th and his fantasy points 10th, even though few quarterbacks are producing more per snap. The Ravens rank second in pass EPA and fourth overall on offense, and he is the reason.

The shape of his game has shifted. He has run 19 times in four games, and only six of those were designed runs. Ten were scrambles, which paid off well: 107 yards, six first downs and +0.48 EPA apiece. His carries went 7, 4, 6, then 2 in Week 4. After a 2025 in which his rushing fell to 349 yards and he took sacks on 43.9% of pressures (53rd of 64), this is a different, more pocket-centered Jackson. His pressure-to-sack rate is back to 26.3%, much closer to his 2024 form than to last year's. The long 3.11-second time to throw and the 6.8% sack rate are the cost of extending plays, and so far the extensions are worth it.

Some of the passing efficiency will fade. His 8.29 CPOE is nearly four points above his career best (4.55 in 2024). He has +0.904 EPA per attempt on 15 intermediate throws and +0.745 on 18 deep shots that he completed less than half the time. Zay Flowers is producing 1.46 EPA per target on 19 looks. These are small samples running hot. Two cooler spots point the other way. On third down his success rate is 34.8%, and the average distance to go is 9.2 yards. In the red zone his EPA is slightly negative despite four touchdowns. When Baltimore leads by nine or more, he plays conservatively (-0.152 EPA), which reflects game script rather than a flaw.

The real issue is availability. He played only 52% of the snaps in Week 4, and the ankle news came the next day. Minter said he doesn't know Jackson's chances and is still waiting on imaging. The line in front of him is also thinning: starting guard Jovaughn Gwyn (91% of snaps) went to injured reserve, center Ethan Pocic is on IR, and left tackle Ronnie Stanley is questionable. If he plays at Atlanta, expect less running and a heavier load on his arm against a defense that shuts down the run.

strengths.title: League-best yardage per dropback
strengths.body: He leads every qualifier in ANY/dropback and is second in yards per attempt, while still keeping his interception rate low. The cause is accuracy plus willingness to push the ball: his intended air yards sit at 10.25 and he is completing far above expectation. The skill is real, since he ranked second in YPA in 2024 too. The exact level is not; expect it to settle closer to his 2024 numbers.

strengths.title: Short-area passing is a machine
strengths.body: On 49 throws under 10 air yards he has a 69% success rate, +0.504 EPA per attempt and five of his six touchdowns. That kind of underneath efficiency is the most repeatable part of a passing profile, and it keeps the offense on schedule. Opponents can't simply sit deep and wait.

strengths.title: Scrambles that pay for the sacks
strengths.body: He has scrambled on 9% of dropbacks and turned those 10 plays into six first downs at +0.48 EPA each. That is the payoff for a time to throw above three seconds. His pressure-to-sack rate has also recovered from last year's bottom-tier mark, so the extending is creating more than it costs again.

concerns.title: Ankle and a depleted interior line
concerns.body: He played 52% of the snaps in Week 4 and is questionable, and his coach is openly unsure. Even if he plays, a guard who logged 91% of snaps is on IR, the backup center is on IR, and Stanley is listed. An ankle that limits his mobility behind a reshuffled interior hits the part of his game that offsets his long time to throw.

concerns.title: Hot downfield samples will cool
concerns.body: His intermediate and deep EPA come from 33 combined throws, and his CPOE is far above anything in his career. Flowers' 1.46 EPA per target is not a rate any receiver holds. Expect the per-dropback numbers to drift down toward his 2024 level, which was still very good.

concerns.title: Third down and red zone lag
concerns.body: His third-down success rate is 34.8%, partly because he is facing 9.2 yards to go on average. His red-zone CPOE is -7. The red-zone touchdowns have come anyway, but both splits are where a cooling passer gets exposed. The samples are small, at 23 and 15 plays.

trend.note: His passing EPA has been at or above +10 in three of four games, with the Week 2 loss to New Orleans the only dip. The rushing has trailed off: two carries in a half-game Week 4 before the ankle news.

nextGame.headline: Atlanta smothers the run; his arm has to carry Baltimore
nextGame.body:
Atlanta's defense is built to stop exactly what Baltimore leans on. It ranks first in rush EPA allowed, second in explosive-run rate and third in success rate. Expect Derrick Henry to grind, and Baltimore's below-expectation pass rate may need to rise. The passing matchup is softer. Atlanta is 10th against the pass, 27th in sack rate, and gives up 273 yards a game to quarterbacks (24th). That suits a 3.11-second holder who has been sacked on 6.8% of dropbacks. On the other side, Atlanta has the league's worst offense and worst passing attack, and its QB room is in flux with Cooper Rush inactive by coach's decision.

Everything hinges on Jackson's ankle. Minter is waiting on imaging. A limited Jackson loses the scramble value that covers his sacks, and he would be playing behind an interior line missing Gwyn, with Stanley and Vorhees listed and Chris Moore out at receiver. Atlanta has its own questions: edge rusher Za'Darius Smith (concussion) and left tackle Jake Matthews (groin) both left their last game. Smith's absence would further thin a pass rush that already rarely finishes sacks.

keyMatchups.title: Henry vs the league's top run defense
keyMatchups.body: Atlanta allows -0.312 EPA per rush and almost nothing explosive. Baltimore's run game is already only eighth in EPA. If early downs stall, Jackson faces more of the long third downs where he has struggled this year.

keyMatchups.title: Time to throw vs a soft rush
keyMatchups.body: Atlanta finishes few sacks (27th in sack rate), which helps a passer who holds the ball. Its deep defense ranks eighth, though, so the downfield shots that have been running hot may meet more resistance.

keyMatchups.title: Atlanta's offense can't keep pace
keyMatchups.body: Atlanta ranks 32nd in offensive EPA and 32nd in passing EPA. It runs well (fifth) against a Baltimore run defense ranked 27th, which points to a slow, ground-heavy game script. That caps Jackson's attempts but keeps him out of catch-up mode.

nextGame.watch: Whether Jackson practices fully this week, and if he plays, whether he scrambles at all early. A Jackson who won't leave the pocket is a much more ordinary passer behind this line.

restOfSeason.body:
The foundation is sustainable. His short-area accuracy, a pressure-to-sack rate back near his 2024 form, and a top-two pass offense all held up across his best seasons. What will regress is the ceiling on the per-play numbers: a CPOE nearly four points above his career best and explosive intermediate and deep EPA on tiny samples. Expect him to look like a top-five passer by efficiency rather than a historic one, still on modest attempt totals because Baltimore leans run.

The rushing is the bigger question. Designed runs have nearly disappeared, so his ground production depends on scrambles, and those depend on a healthy ankle. If the ankle lingers, his fantasy value drifts toward that of a pocket passer on 24 attempts a game. If it clears, 35-plus rushing yards a week remains realistic.
swingFactors: Interior line health with Gwyn out until December
Whether Baltimore's pass rate rises when the run stalls

bets.reason: He is nursing an ankle injury his coach can't yet assess, he has only six designed runs all season, and Atlanta allows the fewest rushing EPA and the second-fewest explosive runs in the league.
Atlanta has the league's worst offense and passing attack, plus a top-eight defense that shuts down the run. Both teams lean run (Atlanta is 30th in pass rate over expected), which shortens the game.

bets.lean: BAL -2.5 if Jackson is confirmed active
bets.reason: A short spread against an offense ranked 32nd in EPA undervalues Baltimore's second-ranked passing attack if Jackson plays. The number likely reflects his questionable tag, so the edge exists only once he is cleared.

confidence.note: Four games and 96 attempts, inflated efficiency, and an unresolved ankle injury cloud the near term.
